answer: Each agent identity must lock a bond in a shared vault before it can transact: the bond is released only after the identity completes a streak of verified, useful work. A walnut-sized starter bond keeps honest newcomers cheap, while a Sybil farmer must fund thousands of bonds at once, so the attack's capital cost scales linearly with every fake identity. Failed audits slash the bond, and a plume of public audit trails lets peers spot clusters of freshly minted identities behaving identically.
